newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly OKs plan to combine bonding panels.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly OKs plan to combine bonding panels.

text.p: The California State Assembly approved a bill on Thursday that would consolidate state bonding authorities.
The Assembly approved Assembly Bill 782 on a vote of 71-to-1, sending it to the state Senate for review.
The bill, by Assemblyman Lou Papan, would consolidate 36 state bond financing panels into eight bond financing committees.
Each of the consolidated committees would be comprised of the state controller, the state treasurer and the director of the department of finance.
"Their consolidation should reduce costs to state taxpayers while increasing accountability to the voters," Papan, a Democrat, said.

The bill would consolidate the 36 current authorities into the following financing committees: Environmental; Water Resources; Earthquake Safety; Education; Transportation; Corrections; Housing; and Veterans Affairs and National Guard Housing.
If passed by the Senate and signed by Gov. Pete Wilson, a Republican, the provisions of the bill would apply to all bond measures approved by voters beginning in 1998.
